title: Define per-endpoint quality contracts and stability allowance policy
creator: Priya Shah
description: Create a canonical policy and artifact set for defining per-endpoint quality contracts (SLO/SLA) and introduce the concept of 'Stability Allowance' — an explicit, time-boxed component of the error budget that coordinates multi-region failovers, circuit-breaker triggers, and preemptive load-shedding thresholds.
background: We currently have many endpoint-level SLO drafts across repos and runbooks with inconsistent definitions for availability and request-quality SLIs (latency P50/P95, model-quality regressions, and token-generation errors). During recent regional incidents, teams applied ad-hoc failover and throttling rules that were hard to reason about and caused customer regressions. The Stability Allowance construct aims to unify how short-term exceptional events are budgeted and remediated while preserving long-term error-budget accounting.
scope: This ticket covers the policy doc, canonical SLI definitions for text-generation and embedding endpoints, a matrix mapping SLI breaches to automated actions (region failover, variant fallback, queueing/circuit-breaker), and a short runbook for on-call. Implementation of automated enforcement is out-of-scope; follow-up tickets will implement hooks in the routing and rate-limiter services.
acceptance_criteria: A single policy document exists that defines Stability Allowance and shows examples with math for monthly error-budget allocation
Canonical SLI definitions for endpoints: chat/generation, embeddings, reranking, and streaming are documented with measurement queries and aggregation windows
A decision matrix maps percent-of-error-budget-burn (and stability-allowance consumption) to concrete automated actions and recommended human escalations
Runbook with step-by-step instructions for oncall to apply manual overrides during an emergent cross-region incident
Stakeholder sign-off (PM, Design for UX messages, Security for audit implications) obtained and recorded
tasks: Draft policy RFC describing Stability Allowance, examples, and allocation algorithm
Define canonical SLI measurement queries for generation/embedding routes and observational caveats
Design action matrix that ties burn-rate thresholds to failover/fallback/load-shed behaviors
Run tabletop with Platform, Routing, and Observability teams and capture feedback
Incorporate feedback, produce final policy doc, and obtain approvals
Publish doc in Confluence and link to relevant dashboards and runbooks
decisions: Use 28-day rolling window for primary SLO computation per endpoint (decided in 2025-03-05 sync)
Stability Allowance will be a 2-tier construct: transient allowance (<= 2 hours) and extended allowance (<= 72 hours) with separate accounting
Circuit-breaker triggers will be aligned to burn-rate thresholds rather than raw latency percentiles to better capture volumetric incidents
Multi-region failover policy defaults to local-region first, then region-pool fallback order defined per-customer tier
Manual override remains available to oncall via /admin/failover but must create an audit event linked to the Stability Allowance ledger
